name: SC-04
label: Likely R

key_factors: Incumbent Timmons with large fundraising advantage
Democrat McClain minimally funded with almost no cash
model.rationale: The district's R+11 lean, Timmons's incumbency and roughly $1.6 million raised against a Democrat with about $33,000 and little cash on hand all point to a comfortable Republican hold, and prediction markets price a Republican win around 94%. With no polls or expert ratings available, the fundamentals-based estimate of a 15-point Republican margin stands.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending against Timmons could narrow the margin, but nothing currently signals a competitive race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Carolina's 4th District leans heavily Republican, and incumbent William Timmons is seeking another term after clearing his primary. He has raised about $1.6 million and benefits from roughly $487,000 in outside support, while Democratic challenger Courtney McClain has raised only about $33,000 and had just over $1,200 on hand. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot with negligible funding.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and money. Prediction markets give Timmons about a 94% chance of winning. The expected result is a Republican victory by roughly 15 points, consistent with the district's partisan lean and the incumbent's advantages.
